source.content: Punkt, the Switzerland-based, privacy-focused phone maker, is trying the whole "smartphone" thing again. The MC03 improves on some of the disappointing features of its previous effort, the MC02, while maintaining its security focus. Likewise, its software still comes with a subscription fee: the first year is included free, but it's $12 per month after that. On top of that, the MC03 is Punkt's first phone to be assembled in Europe rather than Asia, making good on its promise from earlier this year. The MC02, released last year, wasn't exactly a critical darling. Punkt seems to be addressing some of those criticisms with a more modern 6.67-inch display and better specs.

test_cases.description: PRODUCTION FAILURE: Kia EV2 car - automotive, not tech

source.title: Kia Unveils Compact and Affordable EV2 for European Market
source.summary: Kia introduces the EV2, a new compact electric vehicle targeting the European market with an affordable price point
source.content: Kia has officially unveiled the EV2, a new compact electric vehicle designed specifically for the European market with an emphasis on affordability and practicality. The South Korean automaker is positioning the EV2 as an accessible entry point into electric mobility, with pricing expected to significantly undercut many competitors in the compact EV segment. The EV2 showcases Kia's latest design language, featuring sleek LED lighting elements, aerodynamic body panels, and a modern silhouette that aligns with the company's recent electric vehicle lineup. The vehicle's exterior design prioritizes efficiency, with careful attention paid to reducing drag coefficients to maximize range. Inside, the EV2 offers a minimalist yet functional interior layout. The cabin features a digital instrument cluster behind the steering wheel and a central touchscreen infotainment system that supports smartphone integration through Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Seating accommodates five passengers comfortably, with rear seats that fold down to expand cargo capacity for practical everyday use. Built on Kia's dedicated E-GMP electric vehicle platform, which also underpins several other models in the company's EV portfolio, the EV2 benefits from the platform's inherent advantages in packaging and efficiency. The skateboard-style battery placement allows for a flat floor and optimized interior space despite the vehicle's compact exterior dimensions. Range estimates for the EV2 suggest approximately 300 kilometers on a single charge under WLTP testing conditions, with the vehicle supporting DC fast charging capabilities that can replenish the battery from 10 to 80 percent in under 30 minutes. Kia has not yet disclosed the exact battery capacity or motor specifications, but industry observers expect the vehicle to offer adequate power for urban and suburban driving scenarios. The automaker plans to begin deliveries of the EV2 in European markets during the second half of 2026, with production taking place at Kia's European manufacturing facilities. The company is targeting urban drivers, young professionals, and families seeking a practical and affordable electric vehicle for daily commuting and local transportation needs. Kia views the EV2 as a strategic component of its broader electrification roadmap, which aims to substantially increase the proportion of electric vehicles in its overall sales mix by the end of the decade. The company has committed to launching multiple new EV models across various segments to meet evolving consumer demand and increasingly stringent European emissions regulations. Industry analysts suggest that the EV2's competitive pricing could help Kia capture significant market share in the rapidly growing compact electric vehicle segment. As European governments continue to implement stricter emissions standards and offer incentives for electric vehicle adoption, affordable options like the EV2 are expected to play a crucial role in accelerating the transition away from internal combustion engines. The EV2 will face competition from other compact electric vehicles offered by both established automakers and new market entrants, creating a highly competitive landscape in this segment.

source.title: The iPhone Gets a D– for Repairability
source.summary: It's a better rating than the company has gotten from repairability experts before, at least. Samsung is second worst with a D.
source.content:
The iPhone is the least fixable phone on the market, according to repairability experts. Phones from Samsung and Google are not far behind.

The latest repairability ratings are from an annual report called "Failing the Fix" put out today by the consumer advocacy group US PIRG. A 2021 French law required products to be labeled with repairability scores, and US PIRG says this is the first report since then that really shows which companies are—or are not—making progress.
